claims.qualification: Map structure depends on corpus, embedding and clustering choices; the representation is analytical rather than a natural taxonomy of science.
claims.text: A 60-topic grant-based map provides a cross-disciplinary baseline for comparing EU funding portfolios and scientific specialisation.

claims.qualification: A single-country institutional study; causal attribution among Brexit, investment and procurement is not experimentally identified.
claims.text: Reduced market scale and weak domestic investment reinforced UK dependence on US cloud providers and constrained bargaining power.

claims.qualification: A proposal and launch, not an evaluation; effectiveness is explicitly still to be tested.
claims.text: A practical assessment framework has been created for animal research governance committees, together with a research programme to evaluate whether it changes committee practice.

claims.qualification: Stated preferences over hypothetical offers may diverge from actual migration behaviour; one country and one career stage, and the finding concerns willingness to stay rather than availability of suitable positions.
claims.text: PhD students in Italy, including high research performers, prefer to remain despite adverse conditions; salary alone is not the primary determinant of migration decisions, and staying is often framed as accepting a salary or career penalty to continue research.

claims.qualification: Repository version precedes the journal publication; results should be read as the same work's legitimate manuscript version.
claims.text: AI adoption alone is insufficient; complementary structural capabilities shape firms' ability to convert it into gains.

claims.qualification: Findings are specific to a young EU financing instrument whose practices may continue to evolve.
claims.text: Direct public equity creates new governance relationships and steering mechanisms in EU innovation finance.

claims.qualification: The framework is specific to neoclassical realism; the scenarios demonstrate use but do not establish predictive superiority over alternative approaches.
claims.text: The paper maps six traditions from 265 works and proposes an eight-question abductive guide demonstrated across four scenarios.

claims.qualification: Abstract only; the evidence base and the central and eastern European element of the argument are unverified.
claims.text: European strategic autonomy is limited chiefly by structural deficiencies in defence production networks and uneven industrial capabilities rather than by insufficient political ambition.

claims.qualification: Conceptual argument rather than measured outcomes; explanatory rather than predictive.
claims.text: Europeanisation processes and contested European identity impose structural limits on defence integration that funding commitments alone do not resolve.

claims.qualification: Only six experts completed the exercise, so the comparison between methods rests on a very small sample.
claims.text: The two elicitation methods produced broadly similar decision conclusions, while including expert opinion markedly reduced decision uncertainty.

claims.qualification: Ecological observational analysis cannot establish patient-level or causal effects, and some results are sensitive to modelling and stationarity choices.
claims.text: Higher health-AI research capacity was not consistently associated with better equity-adjusted patient value; associations varied by outcome, financial protection and period, with a more favourable treatable-mortality relationship after 2020.

claims.qualification: A single national Delphi exercise on one policy domain; the accuracy verdict may not generalise to other topics or panel designs.
claims.text: Delphi experts predicted the continuation of existing trends accurately but failed to anticipate discontinuities in drug markets and substance popularity.

claims.qualification: A review rather than new empirical work; Europe is one of four comparators, not the study's subject.
claims.text: Regulatory readiness for photovoltaic waste differs markedly across the four jurisdictions, with significant gaps remaining.

claims.qualification: A literature-based synthesis; the integrated approach is not empirically evaluated against alternative planning methods.
claims.text: Backcasting's scholarly and planning strands can be combined into one operational approach for setting and working back from long-horizon strategic goals.

claims.qualification: Method is documented and reusable, but long-horizon foresight remains judgement-intensive.
claims.text: The methodology combines weak-signal scanning, expert participation and transparent assessment to explore transformative technologies over 20 years.

claims.qualification: Operational measures and empirical validation remain to be developed further.
claims.text: Combining deliberation with perspectival realism provides criteria for more plural and accountable foresight.

claims.qualification: Contrastive case design rather than a symmetrical comparison; the secondary cases are used illustratively.
claims.text: Foresight methods are institutionally embedded: identical methods serve expert prioritisation, strategic positioning, stakeholder legitimacy or early warning depending on the governance logic.

claims.qualification: Findings are structured expert expectations rather than forecasts or empirical results, and participants were selected for existing engagement with post-growth and sustainability topics.
claims.text: Experts expect many current trends to obstruct strong sustainability in Europe, while judging that intervention points exist and that desirable post-growth alternatives remain reachable, notably through democratic stewardship of nature.

claims.qualification: Policy-mix coherence depends on participant judgements and assumptions used in morphological analysis.
claims.text: The method combines participatory foresight, X-curve transition mapping and morphological consistency analysis to construct policy mixes.

claims.qualification: Demonstrated in two Living Labs; the authors show feasibility rather than comparative effectiveness against alternatives.
claims.text: A three-part participatory foresight framework successfully converted community narratives into weighted, prioritised climate-resilience pathways in two contrasting European cities.

claims.qualification: Cross-sectional and associational; the study reports associations and spending differences rather than establishing causation.
claims.text: International collaboration is significantly associated with higher web technology adoption, and structural network access is more strongly linked to adoption than relational intensity.

claims.qualification: Describes ambition and architecture rather than demonstrated outcomes; regulatory acceptance is a goal, and the authors themselves flag semantic interoperability and cross-border scaling of federated AI as unresolved.
claims.text: The project presents a modular, standards-based federated platform using privacy-by-design analytics, with lung cancer as its demonstrator, and aims at regulatory and health technology assessment acceptance of real-world evidence.

claims.qualification: Document and indicator synthesis, not causal estimation; results taken from captured abstract text rather than verified full text.
claims.text: Structural and investment constraints, rather than regulation as such, are identified as the main limits on scaling and commercialisation.

claims.qualification: Correlational bibliometric evidence; novelty is proxied by keyword combinations, so the finding depends on that operationalisation.
claims.text: Collaboration is negatively associated with novelty and funded papers are less novel than unfunded ones, though funding moderates the collaboration-novelty link.

claims.qualification: Only part of the abstract was recoverable, so no strong claim about the article's conclusions should be made.
claims.text: Treats AI content labelling as a legal-technical infrastructure; the article's detailed conclusions could not be recovered.

claims.qualification: Framework Programme timing is associational; the design does not establish programme funding as the cause of collaboration changes.
claims.text: European collaboration intensified but retained a hierarchy centred on EU-14, with weaker integration for EU-13 and candidate countries.

claims.qualification: Model-oriented policy study; implementation effects are not established.
claims.text: The paper positions Ukraine’s academy research institutes within a structural model for integration into the European Research Area.

claims.qualification: No primary data, no counterfactual and no performance measurement; conclusions are interpretive and cannot support causal claims.
claims.text: AI is associated with stronger competitive positioning only when combined with financial management capability, digital maturity and responsible governance.

claims.qualification: The study is qualitative and context-specific to five collaborations; it identifies recurring mechanisms and inequalities rather than estimating general population effects.
claims.text: European collaborators disproportionately shaped research approaches, while African collaborators adapted more often and faced barriers to equal participation and visibility.

claims.qualification: Scenarios are exploratory and expert-derived; the method is demonstrated on one project rather than independently validated.
claims.text: A combined multi-level-perspective and PESTLE structure can operationalise vulnerability in participatory scenario building, yielding three exploratory 2050 scenarios per sector.

claims.qualification: The publisher classifies the work as an Opinion Piece; it offers governance arguments and practical considerations rather than evaluated implementation outcomes.
claims.text: Research security should be integrated with integrity, ethics and open-research governance through coordinated system leadership rather than treated as standalone compliance.

claims.qualification: A rapid rather than full systematic review, and it maps reported practice rather than evaluating method performance.
claims.text: Patent analysis is widely used for trend detection in health technology horizon scanning, but inconsistent deduplication and reporting undermine comparability and risk data inflation.

claims.qualification: Framework-development study; performance will depend on implementation context and scanning capacity.
claims.text: MIST combines MedTech development stages, regulatory milestones and weak-signal sources within a Three Horizons structure.

claims.qualification: A normative legal proposal about how the Act should be interpreted, not a court-tested or officially adopted allocation.
claims.text: Duties should follow control and capability, placing transparency and safety obligations upstream with foundation model providers and risk management and oversight downstream with adapters and deployers.

claims.qualification: Aggregate indicators cannot capture every institutional mechanism behind national conversion efficiency.
claims.text: Large cross-country differences persist between R&D effort and innovation-output performance.

claims.qualification: Relies on an existing composite index and secondary data; comparisons are descriptive rather than causal, and the study proposes no new measurement approach.
claims.text: Romania's aggregate entrepreneurial and innovation performance is constrained by specific weak pillars, with entrepreneurial education, clusters and public policy identified as persistent gaps despite EU funding.

claims.qualification: The interoperability model is a policy proposal; it is not an implemented system and the paper does not evaluate observed governance effects.
claims.text: The paper identifies fragmented oversight of dual-use biotechnology and proposes stronger EU–NATO civil-military interoperability for biosecurity governance.

claims.qualification: Small cross-national sample across two years; associations only, with no causal identification.
claims.text: Research and development intensity was the only factor consistently positively significant; cyber diplomacy capacity was not significant.

claims.qualification: The abstract does not report the number or composition of the clusters, so the typology itself cannot be verified.
claims.text: Cluster analysis separates universities into groups differing in funding volume, project involvement and coordinating role.

claims.qualification: Associational regional design cannot prove causal effects of adding universities or institutes; programme-era coverage also shapes the sample.
claims.text: University and research-institute counts are significant predictors of spin-off numbers, with strong concentration in Bucharest-Ilfov.
